places.caption: Real photo: NASA's Curiosity rover (Mastcam), 25 Sept 2015. Colours adjusted to look like daylight on Earth.
places.fact: Curiosity's visit here was the first up-close study of active sand dunes anywhere except Earth. The wind pushes these dunes up to about 1 meter a year.
places.source: NASA Image and Video Library: PIA19928 and PIA20283 captions

places.caption: Real photo: NASA's Curiosity rover (Mastcam), released 4 Oct 2012.
places.fact: Curiosity scooped its first Mars soil at this sandy patch. Heated in the rover's oven, the soil gave off water: about 2% of its weight.
places.source: NASA Image and Video Library: PIA16204; Leshin et al. (2013), Science 341, 1238937 (1.5 to 3 wt% water)

places.caption: Real photo: NASA's Curiosity rover (Mastcam), released 15 Jan 2013.
places.fact: Curiosity drilled its first rock here, at a spot called John Klein. The rock formed in an ancient freshwater lake that could once have supported tiny microbes.
places.source: NASA Image and Video Library: PIA16701, PIA17595; NASA JPL news (2013): 'NASA Rover Finds Conditions Once Suited for Ancient Life on Mars'
